data.name: Malvina
data.gender_notes: Malvina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'mollis' meaning 'soft'. In Christian tradition, Malvina is the name of a saint and is associated with gentleness, kindness, and tenderness. The name Malvina carries the meaning “Gentle, kind, or soft” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Malvina usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, kind, or soft and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Malvina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, kind, or soft.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Malvina total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: מלווינה
in_hebrew.meaning: מלווינה היא שמה של אישה שמקורה בארמית ומשמעותו 'רבת הבנים'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מלווינה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בארמית ומשמעותו 'רבת הבנים' או 'אישה עם הרבה בנים'. השם מורכב מהמילים 'מל' ו'וינה', שפירושם 'מלא' ו'בנים'. השם מוזכר במסורת הנוצרית כבעל משמעות רוחנית עמוקה, הקשורה לברכה ופריון.

in_greek.name: Μαλβίνα
in_greek.meaning: Το Μαλβίνα σημαίνει 'πλούσια σε παιδιά' ή 'αυτή που έχει πολλούς γιους'
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Μαλβίνα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την αρμενική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'πλούσια σε παιδιά' ή 'αυτή που έχει πολλούς γιους'. Το όνομα έχει βαθιά πνευματική σημασία στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, συμβολίζοντας τη γονιμότητα και την πνευματική παραγωγή.

in_latin.name: Malvina
in_latin.meaning: Malvina means 'rich in children' or 'having many sons'
in_latin.long_meaning: Malvina is a Christian name derived from Aramaic roots, signifying 'rich in children' or 'having many sons'. Historically, the name has been associated with virtues of motherhood and piety.

historical_references.reference: Malvina, the daughter of King Belisarius of Sicily, was venerated as a martyr in the 11th century after she was believed to have been killed by the Saracens during an attack on her monastery on the island of Malta.
historical_references.context: During the medieval period, Malta was a center of Christian monasticism and faced frequent attacks from the Saracens.

historical_references.reference: Saint Malvina, a British princess of the 5th century, was supposedly carried off by pirates to the Isle of Man and converted the inhabitants to Christianity. She is now the patron saint of the Isle of Man.
historical_references.context: The Isle of Man was inhabited by pagans and had no formal religious organization until Saint Malvina's arrival.
